subsection: H. Directors and Officers Liability (D&O) Insurance
text: [See Biltmore Assocs., LLC v. Twin City Fire Ins. Co. (9th Cir. 2009) 572 F3d 663, 668 (applying Ariz. law)] But the exclusion is not limited to collusive suits. Rather, it precludes coverage for any internal dispute between the corporation and its officers or directors, as well as for disputes between or among them personally. [American Med. Int'l, Inc. v. National Union Fire Ins. Co. of Pittsburgh (9th Cir. 2001) 244 F3d 715, 723 (applying Calif. law); Level 3 Communications, Inc. v. Federal Ins. Co. (7th Cir. 1999) 168 F3d 956, 958 (applying Neb. law)] (2) [3:692] Wrongful termination claims by former officer? It is unclear whether the insured vs. insured exclusion bars coverage for wrongful termination and breach of contract claims by former corporate officers against the corporation. The dispositive issue appears to be whether the former officer is suing in the former officer's capacity as an “insured” (i.e., officer or director). [See Foster v. Kentucky Housing Corp. (ED KY 1994) 850 F.Supp. 558, 561 (applying Ky. law)—exclusion applicable; compare Conklin Co., Inc. v. National Union Fire Ins.
